item.spade.name: Spade
item.spade.desc: A digging spade, its handle worn smooth by hands. The soil behind the commune house is soft: digging is a pleasure.
item.watering_can.name: Watering can
item.watering_can.desc: A tin watering can with a rose on the spout. You fill it at the rain barrel, and it sounds like a little shower.
item.garden_compost.name: Compost
item.garden_compost.desc: A small sack of compost from the hardware shop. It smells of a wood after rain. Dig it into the bed.
item.seeds_radish.name: Radish seeds
item.seeds_radish.desc: A paper packet with a picture of a red radish on it. Radishes are in a hurry: you only wait a few days.
item.seeds_dill.name: Dill seeds
item.seeds_dill.desc: A packet of dill. Cut it and it grows back, up to three times a summer.
item.seeds_sunflower.name: Sunflower seeds
item.seeds_sunflower.desc: Big striped seeds for sowing, not for nibbling. Though one won't hurt.
item.seed_potatoes.name: Seed potatoes
item.seed_potatoes.desc: A string bag of small potatoes with pale sprouts. Each one is asking to go in the ground.
item.seedling_tomato.name: Tomato seedlings
item.seedling_tomato.desc: Little plants in paper cups, from the market. Rub a leaf and it smells of summer.
item.seedling_strawberry.name: Strawberry runners
item.seedling_strawberry.desc: Strawberry runners with roots, in a cup of soil. Plant them once and they fruit for years.
item.radish.name: Radishes
item.radish.desc: A bunch of radishes from your own bed. Crunchy, with a little bite.
item.dill.name: Bunch of dill
item.dill.desc: Fresh dill. It smells so good you start wanting boiled potatoes.
item.potatoes.name: Potatoes
item.potatoes.desc: New potatoes, still earthy. The skin comes off at a touch.
item.tomatoes.name: Tomatoes
item.tomatoes.desc: Tomatoes still warm from the sun. With salt and black bread, nothing better.
item.strawberries.name: Strawberries
item.strawberries.desc: A handful of strawberries from the bed. The sweetest one was hiding under a leaf.
item.jam_strawberry.name: Jar of strawberry jam
item.jam_strawberry.desc: Jam made by your neighbour from your strawberries. Gauze tied over the lid, a handwritten paper label: "Strawberry".
garden.weeds.some: A few weeds are coming up.
garden.look.grass: An overgrown patch of the bed. It needs digging first.
garden.look.weedy: Dug, but the weeds are back.

garden.prompt.no_seeds: Nothing to sow. Seeds are at the hardware shop and the market.

garden.prompt.can_empty: The can is empty. Fill it at the barrel.

garden.sow.title: What to sow?
garden.sow.none: No seeds or seedlings in my pockets.
garden.toast.rented: The bed is yours. The house committee wrote you into its book.
garden.toast.no_money: Not enough money: the rent is {0} roubles.
garden.toast.covered: The film is down. It'll be warmer tonight.
garden.toast.dead: This one didn't make it: {0}. It happens.
garden.toast.jam_given: Strawberries handed over. {0} will cook the jam.
garden.toast.jam_ready: A jar of jam on the bench, with a note. From: {0}.
garden.toast.contest_entered: The jar is entered. The jury meets on Sunday.
garden.toast.contest_already: Your jar is already in the contest.
garden.toast.compost: The compost is dug into the bed.
garden.diary.rented: I rented a bed behind the commune house. Now I have a patch of earth of my own.
garden.diary.first_harvest: My first harvest: {0}. I grew it myself.
garden.diary.jam: My neighbour cooked jam from my strawberries. The jar is still warm.
garden.diary.contest: The jam contest: {0}. The whole market smelled of strawberries.
garden.name: The commune house allotments
garden.board.title: House committee. Notice
garden.board.text: A free bed for rent for the season. Rent: {0} roubles. Water only from the rain barrel. No dogs in the allotments. Do not taste other people's strawberries, not even "to check if they're ripe". Chair of the allotment committee: M. Berntsen.
garden.letter.from: The jam contest jury, the market
garden.letter.contest.1: Congratulations! Your strawberry jam has taken first place. The keeper of the scales says it's just thick enough, the honey seller says it's nearly as good as honey, and our young juror ate three spoonfuls and asked for a fourth. Prize: {0} roubles, to be collected at the scales.
garden.letter.contest.2: Congratulations! Your jam came second. Whole berries, clear syrup; our young juror said the winner was "a tiny bit sweeter", but licked your jar clean. Prize: {0} roubles, to be collected at the scales.
garden.letter.contest.3: Congratulations! Your jam came third. The honey seller praised its scent, the keeper of the scales the honest weight of the jar. Prize: {0} roubles, to be collected at the scales.
garden.letter.contest.none: Thank you for your jam! It fell just short of a prize this time, but the whole jury ate the jar down to the bottom. Do bring one next time: they say next year's strawberries will be even better.
line.garden.need.dig.1: Dig the bed first. Soil likes to be woken up.
line.garden.need.dig.2: It's all grass. Take the spade: in half an hour you won't know it.
line.garden.need.sow.1: Dug? Then sow while it's loose. Radish is good to start with.
line.garden.need.sow.2: Bare soil gets bored. Plant some dill at least.
line.garden.need.water.1: Your soil's dry. The can's by the barrel, help yourself.
line.garden.need.water.2: Water the roots, not the leaves. The leaves don't complain anyway.
line.garden.need.weed.1: Weeds are coming up. Pull them while they're small.
line.garden.need.weed.2: Your goosefoot is doing better than anything else. That won't do.
line.garden.need.cover.1: It'll be cold tonight. Pull the film down, don't be lazy.
line.garden.need.cover.2: Cover your bed for the night. My tomatoes are already tucked in.
line.garden.need.uncover.1: The sun's out: roll the film up, or it'll all cook.
line.garden.need.uncover.2: It's a sauna under that film by day. Let them breathe.
line.garden.need.pick.1: Yours is ripe. Pick it before it goes over.
line.garden.need.pick.2: Look, it's ripe. The first harvest tastes best, I promise.
line.garden.need.clear.1: Pull out the dead ones, don't be sorry. You'll need the space.
line.garden.need.clear.2: Lost it? Happens to everyone. Clear it and plant again.
line.garden.season.0.1: Don't hurry in spring. The soil has to warm up; it knows best.
line.garden.season.0.2: Potatoes go in when the bird cherry flowers. My mother used to say so.
line.garden.season.0.3: Spring comes late by the sea. But then summer is kind.
line.garden.season.1.1: In summer water in the evening. In the morning the dew does the work.
line.garden.season.1.2: Strawberries like being picked. The more often, the more they give.
line.garden.season.1.3: Cut the dill from the top, leave the root. It'll grow again.
line.garden.season.2.1: Dig potatoes on a dry day in autumn. Wet ones don't keep.
line.garden.season.2.2: There's a chill coming off the sea. Keep the film handy.
line.garden.season.2.3: Tuck the strawberries in with leaves for winter. They're warm under there.
line.garden.season.3.1: In winter the soil sleeps. So can we.
line.garden.season.3.2: Snow on the bed is the best blanket. Leave it.
line.garden.season.3.3: In winter I read seed catalogues. Like novels, only with happy endings.
line.garden.frost.1: Frost tonight. Pull the film down, or there'll be tears in the morning.
line.garden.frost.2: Clear sky, bright stars: that means frost. Cover your bed.
line.garden.hello.1: Morning, neighbour! I've been here since five, and you've only just woken.
line.garden.hello.2: Ah, the young gardener's here. Good morning.
line.garden.hello.3: What a morning, eh? Just the time for the beds.
line.garden.jam.ask.1: Give me your strawberries. I'll cook it tonight, you'll have it by morning.
line.garden.jam.ask.2: Good berries. I'll cook them my mother's way, no hurry.
line.garden.jam.ready.1: Your jam's on the bench. I skimmed the foam and ate it, sorry.
line.garden.jam.ready.2: The jam's ready. Take it to the contest, it's nothing to be shy of.
line.garden.praise.1: Now that's a harvest! I couldn't do that at your age.
line.garden.praise.2: Things grow well for you. You've got a light hand.
line.garden.gift.1: I hear you've got a bed? Here, have some seeds, I've spares.
line.garden.gift.2: These are for your bed. May they come up well.
